old_caption: The video begins with a close-up shot of an orange slice floating on a vibrant blue liquid, likely water. The orange slice is cut in half, revealing its juicy interior with bright orange flesh and white pith. The orange slice rotates slightly as it settles, causing ripples and bubbles to form around it. The background remains consistently blue, emphasizing the contrast between the orange and the water. The video captures the dynamic movement and the vivid colors, highlighting the freshness and vibrancy of the orange slice against the serene blue backdrop.
original_wisa_caption: The video begins with a close-up shot of an orange slice falling into a vibrant blue liquid, likely water. As the orange slice hits the surface, it creates a splash, sending ripples and bubbles outward. The orange slice is cut in half, revealing its juicy interior with bright orange flesh and white pith. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the interaction between the orange slice and the liquid. The orange slice rotates slightly as it settles, causing more ripples and bubbles to form around it. The background remains consistently blue, emphasizing the contrast between the orange and the water. The video captures the dynamic movement and the vivid colors, highlighting the freshness and vibrancy of the orange slice against the serene blue backdrop.
caption: A circular orange slice floats on a blue water surface, viewed from directly above. Its radial segments and pale pith center are clearly visible, with two small seeds set within the middle. Throughout the excerpt the slice turns slowly, its two seeds swinging from a vertical alignment in the early frames to a horizontal one in the later ones. At the same time it drifts upward within the frame, its top edge rising until it nearly meets the upper border. A tight cluster of air bubbles stays nestled against the lower rim, while scattered bubbles elsewhere appear and vanish. The water behind the slice keeps shifting, with ripples and bright reflections sliding across the surface. The slice's overall size holds steady as it moves.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
